title: 911 key hover-jingle
concept: On hover or click, the ring moves and a 964/993-era Porsche 911 key and its remote fob swing from it as chained damped pendulums under gravity, then settle at their original hanging angles.

source.prompt: Draw an air-cooled Porsche 911 key from the 964/993 years (1989-98): a black-headed key with a plain round badge, and its separate black remote fob, on one steel ring. Make it jingle on hover: the ring is the hinge, the fob and key swing under gravity and settle. Keep all the shading.

params.label: Hover swing
params.help: How far the keys swing when the pointer passes over them.

params.label: Click strength
params.help: How much harder a click swings them than a hover.

params.label: Settle time
params.help: How long until the keys hang still again.

params.label: Swing finish
params.help: Soft keeps swinging longer; Firm calms down sooner.

params.label: Ring tilt
params.help: How much the ring itself rocks on its pin.

params.label: Fob swing time
params.help: Time for the remote to swing out and back once. Longer feels heavier.

params.label: Key swing time
params.help: Keep it quicker than the remote so the two don’t move as one.

params.label: Key response delay
params.help: A short lag before the key reacts, so the two pieces don’t start together.

params.label: Fob colour
params.help: Colour of the remote and the key head. The shading stays.

params.label: Metal edge light
params.help: Brightness of the light catching the metal edges.

params.label: Fob inset shade
params.help: Depth of the shading around the remote’s edge.

params.label: Hanging shadows
params.help: Strength of the shadow the keys cast on the wall.

constraints.why: Gives Firm settle enough time to show a swing before the keys hang still.
The key swings faster than the fob so the two read as separate pieces.
